title: Volcan: hear your code review instead of scrubbing a diff

beats.narration_text: That was Volcan. Built for Alexa+, it lets a blind or low-vision developer review an AI agent's pull request by voice.
beats.visual_action: The cold-open turn has ended. The view scrolls to the top of the live page: the heading Hear your code review instead of scrubbing a diff, For blind and low-vision developers, the silent preview of the Inverted admin check patch, and the label Live MCP server, simulated Alexa+ front end. Not an Alexa skill. GitHub: dry-run. That label stays on screen; the narration does not open with it. On the last sentence Alt and 1 puts the focus ring on Hear this code review. No product turn in this beat.

beats.narration_text: This patch, an inverted admin check, goes to Claude on Amazon Bedrock. Volcan runs on AWS Lambda, with its review state in Amazon DynamoDB. Then a line says how much of the patch the model read.
beats.visual_action: Enter on Hear this code review at the first frame of the beat, before the narrator speaks: the model call starts and the narrator talks over the wait. The silent preview stays drawn and the button shows it is working. No cut and no speed-up: the wait is shown as it happened. The narrator says the answer will print a line saying how much of the patch the model read, and stops; the page then holds, still working, until the answer. When the answer arrives, the page plays the falling earcon the server returned and speaks the server's sentence, finding first, while the words light. The product's own sound and voice are in the mix. The engine meter must read Amazon Bedrock; a take whose meter reads local heuristic, or that shows a fallback reason, is recorded again.

beats.narration_text: Amazon Bedrock on the meter, that coverage line, and the model's full answer.
beats.visual_action: Hold on the engine meter reading Amazon Bedrock and the round trip the page measured. Then the coverage line under the spoken caption, exactly as the page prints it: for this short patch, The model read the whole N-character patch., with N as printed. Then open the details The model's full answer and hold on the model's own words. Nothing is typed over the page; every number on screen is one the page printed.

beats.narration_text: Back on the pull request, request changes stages a review, bound to the head commit Volcan read. Listen.
beats.visual_action: Back to Talk through a real pull request, where the chosen pull request is still open. The review comment is_admin is inverted. goes into the comment box, and Request changes after the narrator stops (or the command request changes followed by that comment, typed with Alt and 4). The page plays its cue and speaks its readback, then Ready to request changes on the pull request, bound to head commit and its first seven characters, with the comment, then Say confirm to submit it, or cancel. State AWAITING CONFIRM, with Confirm and Cancel outlined. The whole turn is in the mix as the product's voice; nothing talks over it.

beats.narration_text: Nothing leaves Volcan until you confirm. Confirm, and listen.
beats.visual_action: Confirm after the narrator stops. The page plays its cue and speaks Understood: confirm., then Dry run. Nothing was sent to GitHub. The head commit is still the commit it read, and the exact request Volcan would send has been recorded. A live send would be refused: no GITHUB_TOKEN is set. State RECORDED, NOT SENT. Midway the view moves to the review pane: outcome recorded and not sent, the live head re-read, and the exact POST request body the server recorded. Nothing talks over the turn.

beats.narration_text: This build has no GitHub token: the pane shows the exact request, recorded and not sent.
beats.visual_action: The page has stopped speaking. Hold on the review pane the view moved to during Confirm: outcome recorded and not sent, the live head re-read, and the exact POST request body the server recorded. No product turn in this beat. The screencast ends on this narration, so its sound reaches to within the generator's 0.65 s tail of beat 7, as the sync gate's content-seam check needs: a window that ends on the page's own speech ends in silence, because the slowest-plus-1-s rule leaves a margin and the re-rendered system voice ends before the browser's.

beats.narration_text: This MCP handshake is a real one with the server under the page. Alexa+ itself has never called Volcan.
beats.visual_action: Evidence, tab Server and MCP: Server reached, with the commit and the model path the live server reports. On the first sentence press Run a real MCP handshake, which sends initialize and tools/list and calls no tool, and hold on the negotiated version 2025-11-25 and the tool list as the page prints them. On the last sentence the connection strip and its Alexa+ box, which reads package built and tested locally, not certified or deployed. Then the closing card. Do not press Replay the documented Alexa+ requests on the live build: each of its three clients calls digest_semantic_diff with the default engine, so one press is three billed Bedrock calls and could run close to a minute.
